label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Subject:** Knocknacarra Tuesday club: good news, and a mistake I need to own

Dear Niamh,

I hope you're well. I wanted to write before Wednesday's review meeting, because I think you should hear some news from me directly.

The numbers have changed a lot since your email of 30 October. In September we were averaging about five children a week. By mid-October we were up to nine, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen. The room upstairs at Knocknacarra library is busy from half three until quarter to five, and the children are settling in well. Declan Moran of the Salthill Book Nook also donated 120 books, mostly for the 6 to 9 age group, and a good number of them are in Irish. The children have been delighted with them.

Some of what's happening has moved me more than I can easily put into a list. One of the Ukrainian sisters who started in October now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of every session, and the younger one follows along with real concentration. And a boy who wouldn't open a book at all in September asked me last week if he could take two home. I told him he could. I think that's what this club is for, and I'd hate to see it stopped just as it's taking off.

I also need to tell you about something I did, and I'd rather you heard it from me than from anyone else. A few weeks ago I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers' market. I got carried away telling her about the club and I said she could come along any Tuesday to take photographs. She's now set her sights on Tuesday 24 November, and she intends to bring a photographer.

I should have checked with you before saying anything at all. I know the policy: no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I was wrong not to check first, and I'm sorry I put you in that position. I don't want to make excuses. I got excited, and I spoke before I thought.

I do think the coverage could be really good for the club, and for the library and the volunteers too, but only if it's done properly and with your agreement. So I'd like to put things right in two ways.

First, I'll ring Orla this week and tell her the visit is on hold. I won't make any arrangement with her until you've decided what you want to do. If you'd prefer that I didn't speak to her at all, just say so and I'll leave it with you.

Second, I'd be very grateful if you could look at the new attendance figures before the meeting on the 18th and reconsider the pause. I'm not trying to tell you how to run the programme. You know far better than I do what the insurance and the wider picture involve, and I trust your judgement. But I would hate for a decision to be made on the basis of the numbers from October, when things look so different now.

If you do decide the photographs can go ahead, I'm happy to collect the consent forms myself and go through them with every family before anything is taken. I'll make sure no child is photographed without a signed form, and I'll send you the list of who has consented before the visit. If you'd prefer no photographs at all, that's fine too, and I'll tell Orla so.

Thank you for your patience with me on this, and for the care you've put into the programme. I'd really like to talk it through with you, whether by phone or over coffee, before Wednesday if that suits you.

Warm regards,

[Your name]
